at_rest_phase.purpose: 0026's rss-gate fixture cares about steady-state serving memory, not only the transient build-time peak -- captured as a natural, low-cost complement to the build measurement (not literally requested by name in RUNBOOK.md step 5, which names 'run_serve/run_build' either driver).
at_rest_phase.command: python3 bench/query.py --server dist/index.js --data-dir <same dir as build_phase> --backend sqlite --queries-file bench/queries.txt --limit 20 --repeat 3
at_rest_phase.note: At-rest RSS (122,7-137,1 MiB) is roughly 15x smaller than the build-time peak (2 046,1 MiB) -- consistent with the SQLite backend being disk-resident rather than memory-resident once built, the same pattern already documented for the capped case in bench/results/json-baseline/SUMMARY.json's comment on 'the SQLite 121-135 MiB column'. The build-time peak, not the at-rest figure, is the number that reproduces 0011's 2 084,9 MiB class.

reproduction_check.target: bench/results/0011-rss/uncapped-build-3.json -- 371,6 s, 1 848,8 MiB peak_rss_kb (1 893 192 kB), 477 512/465 110 passages, measured 2026-08-22 on an earlier (v1.9.0-era) tree
reproduction_check.measured_here: 182,2 s, 2 046,1 MiB peak_rss_kb (2 095 172 kB), 477 511/465 109 passages, measured 2026-08-30 on trunk v1.10.0
reproduction_check.verdict: REPRODUCES THE CLASS. Peak RSS is within 10,6% of the 0011 figure (2 046,1 vs 1 848,8 MiB) and both land inside the '2 084,9 MiB class' the 0025 substrate map names (bench/results/0003-full-build's 339,0 s / 2 084,9 MiB (2 134 916 kB) is the third sibling in that range, 39 744 kB / 38,8 MiB apart from the 2 095 172 kB measured here). Passage counts match to within one item (477 511 here vs 477 512/477 511 across siblings -- the library gains and loses a top-level item between crawls, as already noted in 0011-rss's own provenance).
reproduction_check.elapsed_time_note: 182,2 s here is roughly HALF of 0011's 371,6 s. Not explained by this run -- reported as an observation, cause not established. Candidates not distinguished: trunk v1.10.0 build-path changes since v1.9.0, host-load differences between the two sessions (0011 ran 2026-08-22, this ran 2026-08-30), and filesystem cache state (Zotero's own storage and this run's temp dir may have been warmer in page cache this time). RSS, not wall time, is the figure this experiment exists to reproduce, and RSS agrees closely.
